lastText: File ClosedThe Seam in the WallMinor VictorySoviet High Command, 1941 — 1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) — filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945 — later than the historical May 1945, the price of choices that spent time to save men. The army that reaches Berlin has paid for the ground twice over — a war fought closer to the historical pattern of holding rigid lines regardless of the arithmetic, at the cost this campaign keeps returning to. The push straight for Berlin in February was actually attempted here — testing Chuikov's postwar claim against the flank risk Zhukov's own staff warned about, rather than leaving the question a memoir argument. The autumn 1942 reserve was weighted entirely south — Mars never launched, the Rzhev grinder's cost declined, and the single-theater concentration tested against the pinning argument Mars's defenders always made. Order No. 227 was transmitted but its blocking detachments and penal machinery left to commanders' discretion — the argument some front commanders quietly practiced, made policy here. Berlin's fall was a certainty from the day the front stopped moving west; everything this campaign tracked was the cost of the miles back.One Year LaterVictory arrived behind the historical May 1945, which means Soviet forces are still consolidating a front the historical record had a year's head start settling by this point.
